headline: ChatGPT rolls out verified business agents, US only
dek: Business Agents enter testing for US shops and services, per The Verge.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: What changes
body: ChatGPT will let users chat with verified AI agents that represent companies, per The Verge and TechRadar.
For now it is a beta, only for eligible US businesses (The Verge).

points.t: The agent appears when a firm is in an answer.
It stays apart from the main chat.
Firms sign up in the Business Hub.

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Privacy and ads
body: Chats are not shared with businesses, and data arrives only in aggregate, per TechRadar.
Firms may pay for more prominence, labeled as sponsored (TechRadar).

items.t: OpenAI gave no method details (The Verge).

caption.hook: ChatGPT is getting Business Agents, verified AI agents that represent companies.
body: Per The Verge and TechRadar, the feature is in beta and covers only eligible e-commerce and online-service businesses in the United States. The agent appears when a company shows up in an answer, and the chat with it stays separate from the main conversation.

To build an agent, a company signs up in the Business Hub, sets instructions and tracks performance metrics. TechRadar says chats are not shared with businesses and data arrives in aggregate. Per TechRadar, companies will be able to pay for more prominence, labeled as sponsored content.
